title: Manoeuvring Against Weaknesses
subtitle: The Principle of Two Weaknesses and the Central Pivot
summary: The art of positional manoeuvring: shifting pressure between two separated enemy weaknesses and utilizing central outposts as fluid pivots.
aphorism: A single weakness can be defended; two weaknesses separated by the board will tear the defensive fabric apart.
attribution: 100th Anniversary Centenary Edition. Newly authored prose and interactive studies inspired by Aron Nimzowitsch (1925).

body.historicalContext: Nimzowitsch introduced the Principle of Two Weaknesses, demonstrating that positional victory comes from probing back and forth between two distant targets until the defense collapses.

sections.title: The Principle of Two Weaknesses
sections.markdown:
When the opponent has a single static weakness, their army can usually muster enough defenders to hold the line.

To break the impasse, you must apply the **Principle of Two Weaknesses**: create a second weakness on the opposite side of the board! Because your pieces possess greater central [[mobility]], you can pivot between the two targets faster than the defender can shuffle back and forth.

moves.comment: White liquidates to open attacking diagonals.
White launches the second front on the queenside!

drills.title: Open the Second Front
drills.markdown: Black is focused on defending the center. Capture on c5 to open a new highway on the queenside.

hints.text: Play dxc5 to shatter Black's central structure.

feedback.correct: Right! Creating queenside targets stretches Black's defensive resources to the limit.
